merge_request.title: chore(deps): upgrade sqlalchemy 1.4.49 -> 2.1.6
merge_request.description:
Upgrading SQLAlchemy from 1.4.49 to 2.1.6 involved adapting to significant API shifts in query construction, execution patterns, and session management. The `select()` function now requires strictly positional column arguments, while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statements no longer accept keyword-based constructors—both necessitated refactoring across database interaction code. Legacy methods like `Engine.execute()` and `Session.query()` were replaced with modern equivalents using `Connection.execute()` and `Session.execute(select())`, aligning with SQLAlchemy 2.0’s unified Core/ORM approach. The declarative base import moved from `sqlalchemy.ext.declarative` to `sqlalchemy.orm.declarative_base`, and enabling the `future=True` flag on `Session` activated autobegin behavior while removing subtransaction complexity. Result handling was updated to use `.scalars()` and `.unique()` for ORM object extraction, reflecting the new named-tuple-like row semantics. All changes were applied to `pyshop/db.py` and `requirements.txt`, and the full test suite passes, confirming stability and correctness under the new version. ## What changed - sqlalchemy 1.4.49 -> 2.1.6 in requirements.txt ## Code changes and why | File | Change | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | `pyshop/db.py` | declarative_base moved from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative to sqlalchemy.orm in SQLAlchemy 2.0 (breaking change #6).
SQLAlchemy 2.0 requires select() columns to be passed positionally, not as a list (breaking changes #1 and #5).
Replace deprecated Query API with select() and Session.execute() pattern, using scalars() for ORM results.
Replace deprecated Query.get() with Session.get() per SQLAlchemy 2.0 migration guide. | [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#library-level-but-not-driver-level-autocommit-removed-from-both-core-and-orm) [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#declarative-becomes-a-first-class-api) [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#select-no-longer-accepts-varied-constructor-arguments-columns-are-passed-positionally) | ## Documented changes that applied to this codebase - **breaking**: select() no longer accepts varied constructor arguments, columns passed positionally (sqlalchemy.Column, sqlalchemy.select) > The list of columns / tables to SELECT from should be passed positionally, rather than as a list. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#select-no-longer-accepts-varied-constructor-arguments-columns-are-passed-positionally) - **breaking**: insert/update/delete DML no longer accept keyword constructor arguments (sqlalchemy.Column, sqlalchemy.Integer, sqlalchemy.String) > The constructor arguments to insert(), update() and delete() other than the table argument are essentially removed. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#insert-update-delete-dml-no-longer-accept-keyword-constructor-arguments) - **breaking**: Engine.execute() considered legacy, use Connection.execute() or Session.execute() (sqlalchemy.create_engine) > The Engine.execute() method is considered legacy as of the 1.x series of SQLAlchemy and will be removed in 2.0. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#library-level-but-not-driver-level-autocommit-removed-from-both-core-and-orm) - **breaking**: Session.query() unified with Core select(), new Session.execute(select(...)) pattern (sqlalchemy.select) > The Query object becomes long term legacy, replaced by the direct usage of the select() construct in conjunction with the Session.execute() method. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#orm-query-unified-with-core-select) - **breaking**: select() legacy calling style deprecated, new positional style required (sqlalchemy.Column, sqlalchemy.select) > The list of columns / tables to SELECT from should be passed positionally, rather than as a list. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#select-no-longer-accepts-varied-constructor-arguments-columns-are-passed-positionally) - **breaking**: Declarative base import path changed from ext to orm (sqlalchemy.ext.declarative.declarative_base) > Change imports: from sqlalchemy.ext import declarative_base, declared_attr To: from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, declared_attr [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#declarative-becomes-a-first-class-api) - **breaking**: Session future flag enables autobegin, removes subtransactions (sqlalchemy.orm.sessionmaker) > The Session no longer supports 'bound metadata' when it resolves the engine to be used for connectivity. This means that an Engine object must be passed to the constructor. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#migration-to-2-0-step-five-use-the-future-flag-on-session) - **breaking**: Result rows act like named tuples, require .scalars()/.unique() for ORM results (sqlalchemy.select) > Result rows act like named tuples and it will not deduplicate results in memory. In order to return single ORM objects the way Query does, the Result.scalars() modifier must be called first. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#result-rows-act-like-named-tuples) - **deprecation**: RemovedIn20Warnings deprecation categories (noise until resolved) > Code can be developed iteratively to resolve these warnings. Enable SQLALCHEMY_WARN_20=1 environment variable. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#migration-to-2-0-step-two-turn-on-removedin20warnings) ## Verification - After the bare version bump: 15 passing, 2 failing of 17 collected - After Upshift's edits: **17 passing, 0 failing of 17 collected** | Attempt | Model | Edits | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 2 | 15 passing, 2 failing of 17 collected | | 2 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 1 | 15 passing, 2 failing of 17 collected | | 3 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 1 | 16 passing, 1 failing of 17 collected | | 4 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 2 | 17 passing, 0 failing of 17 collected | ## Review Verdict: **approve**. No weakened tests, behavior changes, compat shims, missed migrations, or security regressions found. merge_request.description:
Upgrading Pydantic from 1.10.13 to 2.14.1 involved updating code to align with v2’s breaking changes: renamed BaseModel methods and Field parameters, replaced validator decorators with @field_validator, migrated BaseSettings to pydantic-settings, updated ValidationError imports, replaced Config classes with model_config, removed constrained types, and deleted deprecated modules. The changes were applied across pyshop/models.py, pyshop/settings.py, requirements.txt, and tests/test_models.py. All tests pass and the test suite is green. ## What changed - pydantic 1.10.13 -> 2.14.1 in requirements.txt - added pydantic-settings==2.16.1 to requirements.txt ## Code changes and why | File | Change | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | `pyshop/models.py` | Migrated all pydantic v1 APIs to v2: replaced ValidationError import, validator/root_validator with field_validator/model_validator, Config class with model_config=ConfigDict, __root__ with RootModel, const with frozen, allow_mutation with frozen, parse_obj with model_validate, __fields__ with model_fields, dict with model_dump, and updated Field parameters (min_length/max_length, pattern). Used Annotated with StringConstraints for constrained strings. Updated Tags to inherit from RootModel with root field.

merge_request.description:
Upgrading Flask from 2.0.3 to 3.1.3 involved addressing several breaking changes due to internal refactoring, including the removal of `json.JSONEncoder` and `json.JSONDecoder`, deprecation of `json_encoder` and `json_decoder` attributes on apps, renaming parameters in `send_file` as its deprecation period concluded, migrating from `LocalStack` to context variables for app and request contexts, restructuring the sans-IO base classes for `Flask` and `Blueprint`, and updating imports of `escape` and `Markup` to come from `markupsafe` instead of the deprecated Flask reexports. These adjustments were applied to `notes/__init__.py` and `requirements.txt`, after which the full test suite passes without failures. ## What changed - flask 2.0.3 -> 3.1.3 in requirements.txt - click co-upgraded to 8.5.0 in requirements.txt (pip: incompatible with flask 3.1.3) - itsdangerous co-upgraded to 2.2.0 in requirements.txt (pip: incompatible with flask 3.1.3) - jinja2 co-upgraded to 3.1.6 in requirements.txt (pip: incompatible with flask 3.1.3) - werkzeug co-upgraded to 3.1.9 in requirements.txt (pip: incompatible with flask 3.1.3) - added markupsafe==3.0.4 to requirements.txt ## Code changes and why | File | Change | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | `notes/__init__.py` | Migrated all Flask 3.0+ breaking changes: replaced flask.json.JSONEncoder with custom JSONProvider assigned to app.json, moved escape import to markupsafe, removed deprecated JSON_SORT_KEYS config, replaced before_first_request with direct function call during app creation, and kept errorhandler decorators which remain valid.
Replace deprecated `werkzeug.urls.url_quote` import with `urllib.parse.quote` (Werkzeug 3.x deprecates the `werkzeug.urls` module). The custom `DecimalJSONProvider` assigned to `app.json` already matches Flask 3.x's JSONProvider interface (dumps/loads), so no change needed there. The `before_first_request` simulation via immediate `warm_up()` call is the correct migration. The `escape` import from `markupsafe` is already correct per Flask 2.3+ deprecation.
Added the required `response()` method to `DecimalJSONProvider` for Flask 3.x's new JSON provider interface, and moved the warm-up logic to a `before_request` hook so it runs on the first request instead of at app creation time. | [source](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-3-0-0) [source](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-2-3-0) [source](https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/changes) | ## Documented changes that applied to this codebase - **breaking**: json.JSONEncoder and json.JSONDecoder removal (flask.json.JSONEncoder) > `json_encoder` and `json_decoder` attributes on app and blueprint, and the corresponding `json.JSONEncoder` and `JSONDecoder` classes, are removed. [↗](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-3-0-0) - **breaking**: json_encoder and json_decoder attributes removal (flask.json.JSONEncoder) > `json_encoder` and `json_decoder` attributes on app and blueprint, and the corresponding `json.JSONEncoder` and `JSONDecoder` classes, are removed. Migrate Session.query() to Session.execute(select()) with .scalars() for ORM object results.
select() no longer accepts a list argument; pass columns positionally.
Use new Session.get() primary-key lookup API instead of legacy Session.query().get(). | [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#declarative-becomes-a-first-class-api) [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#migration-to-2-0-step-five-use-the-future-flag-on-session) [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#library-level-but-not-driver-level-autocommit-removed-from-both-core-and-orm) | ## Documented changes that applied to this codebase - **breaking**: select() no longer accepts varied constructor arguments, columns passed positionally (sqlalchemy.Column, sqlalchemy.Integer, sqlalchemy.String, sqlalchemy.create_engine, sqlalchemy.select) > The list of columns / tables to SELECT from should be passed positionally. Replace deprecated parse_obj with model_validate for roundtrip test. | [source](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/migration/#changes-to-pydantic-basemodel) | ## Documented changes that applied to this codebase - **breaking**: BaseModel method renames (breaking) (pydantic.BaseModel) > Various method names have been changed; all non-deprecated BaseModel methods now have names matching either the format model_.* or __.*pydantic.__. [↗](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/migration/#changes-to-pydantic-basemodel) - **breaking**: Field property removals/renames (breaking) (pydantic.Field) > Field no longer supports arbitrary keyword arguments to be added to the JSON schema. [↗](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/migration/#changes-to-pydantic-field) - **breaking**: BaseSettings relocation (breaking) (pydantic.BaseSettings) > BaseSettings has moved to a separate package, pydantic-settings. [↗](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/migration/#basesettings-has-moved-to-pydantic-settings) - **breaking**: Config class -> model_config (breaking) (pydantic.BaseModel) > In Pydantic V2, to specify config on a model, you should set a class attribute called model_config to be a dict with the key/value pairs you want to be used as the config.
